# Shape-offer usage fixture

Use the locally available `shape-offer` skill on the context below. Return only
the concise Offer Brief requested by the skill. Do not research, contact anyone,
write files, launch anything, or invent missing evidence.

## Founder context

This is a synthetic scenario; it does not describe a real person or customer.
An instructor teaches sourdough baking from a small home kitchen. They have
three years of teaching experience and currently sell a two-hour, one-to-one
session for 850 DKK. Five people have paid for that session; four later sent a
photo of a loaf they were happy with. The instructor has not asked whether they would buy
again, and they have no other sales or survey data.

The people who book her usually already bake occasionally. They say they are
frustrated that their starter seems active but their loaves are dense and
unpredictable. The instructor believes they want confidence and a repeatable routine,
but she has not tested that wording.

She can spend at most four hours each week on this offer, wants to keep
delivery personal, and does not want paid advertising, countdowns, scarcity,
or a large course library. She is considering a small group format but has not
decided how many people, how long it should run, or what support would be
included. The current 850 DKK price is for the one-to-one session only; no
group price has been chosen. Ingredient costs are small but not recorded.

## Request

Shape the most sensible next offer from this context. Keep evidence separate
from assumptions and unknowns. If the group format or price cannot be decided
without a material answer, identify one question or the smallest validation
that would resolve it. Do not add bonuses, guarantees, urgency, or invented
market demand.
